notes: Source: research/003-stage-pushing-meta/evidence/05-youtube/ (yt-dlp info.json + Korean auto-captions). Captions are auto-generated and noisy; cookie names are normalised only where context is unambiguous, otherwise kept as heard and marked '(caption, unsure)'.
Team rosters and sugar-rune screens in these videos are shown on screen and mostly not spoken. Only what the narration names is recorded here; cookies not named are left out rather than guessed.

ND러너 is a top player (crumb.gg combat-power leaderboard rank 2 as 'ND러너YouTube', about 30G account power on 2026-09-28). He was the third player on all servers to enter the Dimensional Rift. His statements on the Rift and on power are first-hand from the top of the ladder and are weighted accordingly. Note that his own on-stream power figures (for example 4G real / 6G shown on 2026-09-24, about 5G real / 22G shown on 2026-09-26) are Rift-inflated, which likely explains the ~30G crumb.gg figure.

Shorthand in captions: 정갈 = 전갈 (Scorpion), 성류 = 석류 (Pomegranate), 피결/피겨 = Skating Queen, 딸크 = Strawberry Crepe, 딸쇼 = Strawberry Shortcake, 닥초/닼초 = Dark Choco, 체콜 = Cherry Cola, 이혼/이온 = Ion Cookie Robot, 호미/홈밀/코밀 = 호밀 (Rye), 바람수/바람공수 = 바람궁수 (Wind Archer), 시커/부시커/브커 = Brightseeker, 밀키 = Milky Way, 우유 = Milk (Pediatrician), 5분 랩 = 오븐 레벨 (Oven level). 바궁/바공 means Wind Archer in videos from before Princess Bari's release (2026-09-23) and in ND러너's power-inflation advice; 바리/바리공주 means Princess Bari.

posts.title_en: Cookie Run Crumble Dimensional Rift review: a whole new world
posts.summary_en: ND러너's livestream review of the Dimensional Rift right after he cleared 328-30 (Coward Cookie as the final boss) and became the third player on all servers to enter. He explains how the Rift works: per-level rewards, a level-1 pet, daily and season rankings, and the 차원의 힘 level that grows over idle time and inflates power (4G real shown as 6G). He also covers his stage presets, why GingerBright should not be used, how to handle Redberry, and stage accuracy targets. His first Rift attempts against Cool Mint with adds show debuffs failing for lack of focus, and he concludes that raw power decides the Rift too.

mechanics: Relief of 2026-09-23: map difficulty was nerfed and stages got much easier. The final Coward at 328-30 'isn't that strong'. Herb is no longer needed.
The first wall most players hit is 29-30.
Raw power decides fights where damage doesn't land: '깡전투력이 답' (raw power is the answer) in the Rift too.
Moon Rabbit (달토끼) is unnecessary on stages. Use it only if you genuinely can't survive; retrying is better than playing defensively.
Pushing stages early matters more than anything: idle-box rewards give resources money can't buy. 'Stage is the main content; go all in.'
Implant Tower (out of scope): the stage decks work there too, but you must hug the boss manually; players who leave it idle time out.
rift: Unlock: clear main stage 328-30. After the final Coward the story ends and a portal to 차원의 이면 opens. Content is split into seasons (시즌 1).

Level-1 clear reward: a pet, heard as '시간지기' (he also names '무한바퀴' and says 'you must get this'). Effect: ally boss damage +50% inside the Rift. Holding effect: Charge-type evasion +3. Level 10: a profile frame. Every level has its own reward.

Rankings: a server ranking plus an all-server ranking. The Rift appears to be all-server (integrated). There is an entry-order list with timestamps; ND entered third, and eight to nine players had entered on the first night. Rewards: daily ranking (1일 정산) and season ranking, plus a participation reward. The top 10 receive rewards.
Inside the Rift the idle reward per minute increases (only the per-minute count; other rewards are the same).

차원의 힘 level: accumulates per minute while you are in the Rift, levels up and strengthens a buff that inflates power. ND showed 6G inside versus 4G outside. His first read: early entrants have a big advantage, 'the real idle game starts here'.
Structure: the boss comes with adds from both sides from the start (Cool Mint plus mobs). 'Nasty structure.'

First attempts: Cherry Cola needed for damage. Dark Choco's shred debuff didn't land because of too little focus (집중 부족). Rye to sustain. A pouch pet (복주머니; likely 색동 주머니, caption, unsure) was considered. Judge a clear by how fast HP drops in the first seconds.
stage_types: Launch bosses (망치, 쿨링민트, 그루터기, 초코왕방울): swap to the Panda Dumpling pet preset.
Cool Mint: fight in the 7 or 11 o'clock corner. Adds pull aggro and split damage.
Redberry Assassin: the one place the generic deck fails. Swap two melee cookies for Tiger Lily + Rye and lure to the 6 o'clock stairs.
Coward: generic deck plus a high-power filler. No GingerBright.
disagreements: GingerBright (명랑한 쿠키) on Coward: ND says it is acceptable only for complete beginners. At higher stages it lowers team power and therefore damage, and 'makes clearable stages unclearable even for high-spec users'. This contradicts guide makers who build a GingerBright deck for Coward (서신우 2026-08-16, 꽝라멩 2026-09-06).
Early-entrant advantage in the Rift: on 2026-09-24 ND says the first entrants 'win unconditionally'. On 2026-09-26 (yt:BDuQ279mbP4) he softens this: late entrants can overtake if they climb fast.

posts.title_en: Cookie Run Crumble Dimensional Rift level 11 attempt
posts.summary_en: A five-hour stream: ND러너 pushes Rift level 11 and reviews viewer accounts. Rift facts: the 차원의 힘 buff grows with time, so his shown power is 22G against about 5G real (about 4.5x). There is a power cut, there are per-level, daily and season rewards and a level-20 extra, and bosses repeat in fixed patterns. Debuffs and accuracy fail often, so he raised focus. On stages he gives accuracy/focus targets by stage band, says pushing at 35% works fine after the relief (except Redberry), advises not to look at the bracket at all, and ranks gear by power first.

clears.boss: ? (Hammer Princess and a poison-weak boss discussed)
clears.note: At [31:08] he says 'this will definitely clear' after changes; no explicit clear line in captions.
[2:28:41] recalled: 'at 248-30 I wasn't even at 1G'. Date not given (before the relief).
[55:52] 'At 35% it pushes fine, don't worry; the only one I still hate at 35% is Redberry Assassin.'
Viewer stuck because they left it on auto. ND: 'hug it and it pushes right away'.

teams.name: ND stage preset 5, advice given to viewers
pets: three pets. When a launch boss appears (쿨링민트, 망치, 그루터기, 왕초코방울), swap the middle pet for Panda Dumpling.

For the Macaron buff.

pets: 와사비 문어 (Octo Wasabi): he remembers clearing this boss with it
teams.why: Without Herb the Volley (다발) synergy has to come from another slot.

builds.gear: Stages are power-based, so pick gear by power. If power is close, prefer Skill AMP, Skill Haste, DMG Reduction. Crit damage and crit resist lines inflate power a lot. DEF: treat it as 'no option'.
builds.thresholds: [02:45] about 1000 accuracy, 1000–1100; higher is wasted. [1:52:41] 200-stage band: accuracy/focus high-800s minimum. 300+: high-900s minimum. [5:10:06] Before 300: 900+. 300+: minimum '1에서 150' (caption, likely 1000–1050 or 1100–1150, unsure). Very high-spec players clear 300+ at 900 with some misses.
builds.why: Misses also stop debuffs from applying, which is very noticeable in the Rift.

builds.gear: He kept accuracy around 1000 and raised focus further because debuffs weren't landing.
builds.why: 'Dark Choco feels like an empty can' when focus is short. Viewer question: can you drop accuracy/focus gear once the Rift buff raises them? He considered swapping to Skill Haste.

builds.sugar_runes: Skill Haste plus some focus. Needs no amplification.
builds.why: [3:18:25] 'Drop Dark Choco's focus and the debuff doesn't go in at all; it becomes an empty-can Dark.'

builds.gear: Arena: Skill Haste, Skill AMP, DMG Reduction, crit resist. Conquest: Skill AMP, Skill Haste, DMG Reduction plus crit damage/rate; accuracy/focus not needed at all.
builds.why: Given as the contrast to the power-first stage preset.

builds.sugar_runes: Don't lower cookie levels to steer Pomegranate's beam target; maximise power instead.
builds.why: [44:31] The beam target may move around anyway, and it doesn't block clears. Buff targeting goes by ATK, not power.

mechanics: [58:50] Advice on the bracket: don't look at it. ND never checks the 55% cut, because knowing you're below it stops you from even trying. After the relief even 15% might be clearable somehow.
Stages: 'stage is purely power'. If gear lines are close, look at options; otherwise take the higher-power item.

Power growth: the fastest route is gear from Oven levels. Each Oven level-up gives about +300m minimum once the gear is farmed ([3:42:25]). Fame (명성) gives about 18–19m per level at his level and is unbounded. Research: finish HP (체력) and step up one node at a time.
Coward is easy once lab HP research is done. Players who find Coward hard haven't researched HP yet; with HP, Redberry feels harder than Coward.
Don't use sweep (소탕) on daily dungeons: 'throwing money away'.
Evasion experiment: ND plans an all-evasion test. He argues high-stage bosses like the eagle (독수리) always hit the same target, so one or two evasion lines may become useful for stages later.
Focus vs focus rate: the displayed value converts into a skill success chance against the stage's value; crumblehub has a calculator where you enter power, stage and focus.
rift: [03:28] The Rift has a time-based buff that keeps rising, so specs look like they jump day to day. 'That's not real growth.'
[22:50] '투력이 22주 됐잖아요. 원래는 제 실제로는 5주인데 ... 4.5배 거의': shown power 22G versus about 5G real because of the 차원의 힘 buff. Even low-power players get inflated, so entering early is good.
[10:56] Correction: entering first isn't everything. On day one first entrants had the edge, but late entrants can overtake if they can climb fast.
[47:29] '투력컷이 존재하는 거 같아요': a power cut seems to exist; past a certain power the difficulty changes sharply.
[48:16] Rewards per level cleared, profile and pet rewards, a daily settlement (ranks 1–3 and more) and a season settlement. An extra reward at level 20.
[15:20] Bosses repeat in the same patterns ('무한 반복'). Save or screenshot what worked; pre-planned players will push fast. At [4:19:19] he says there are only about four boss types.
[14:44] He expects the next update to add stages while the Rift range stays the same.
[3:21:02] The Rift isn't a 'too hard, give up' place: the buff makes it steadily easier and the reward competition pushes people.
Misses and failed debuffs are much more noticeable in the Rift; he raised focus and considered dropping debuff cookies entirely ([24:24]).
stage_types: Launch bosses (쿨링민트, 망치, 그루터기, 왕초코방울): middle pet to Panda Dumpling.
Redberry (the cookie that blinks and vanishes): remove the melee pair and add Rye + Tiger Lily.
Bosses in general: if damage is short, drag the team onto the boss manually; many stuck viewers had simply left it on auto.
disagreements: Accuracy targets: ND's own target is 1000–1100 for 300+, but he reports a common community view that very high-spec players clear 300+ at 900 with misses.
Early-entrant advantage in the Rift: he reverses his 2026-09-24 claim (yt:_d_7z1UD2p8) that first entrants always win.

posts.title_en: Cookie Run Crumble Dimensional Rift level 16 attempt
posts.summary_en: ND러너 pushes Rift level 16 and reviews accounts. Key claims: every Rift level is tuned like a 35% bracket fight and is designed to become clearable as the time-based buff stacks. Auto never clears and you must build your own decks; the Rift entrance has a Charge buff; the level-20 reward is a pet pass. On stages: 318-18 (Redberry zone) is the last big wall before 328-30, and he gives positioning tips. If damage doesn't land (for example on 318-30 Coward) you are below the 35% bracket: inflate team power with the TSSR Wind Archer and by keeping power-heavy SSR rune lines until you reach the Rift.

clears.note: At [23:20] 'it's not uncrackable; the angle is visible now'. No explicit clear line.

clears.team: viewer deck plus TSSR 바궁 (Wind Archer) for power
clears.note: 'Damage isn't landing, so you're not at 35% yet.' After raising power: 'one-click fix, retry right away'.
ND: the last and biggest wall before 328, 'after this there's nothing hard'. He himself spent hundreds of runs here.

teams.name: ND Rift trial deck (level 16)

cookies.note: 'Strawberry Crepe is a must.'
[21:07] Picked over Scorpion for this level.
[18:49] shown ('다리봉주' = 바리공주, caption).

pets: 와사비 문어 (Octo Wasabi; '팬문어', caption) is clearly better in the Rift
teams.formation: Pull the boss slightly toward 6 o'clock rather than fighting it head-on.
teams.why: 'Heavily affected by pets.' Rapid-fire (연타) synergy is too costly to drop. A cookie that splits damage onto adds is useless.

teams.name: 318-18 Redberry advice

cookies.note: ND recommended it: 'the higher the power, the better the damage lands'.
Needed for the ice-spot burst point.
Keep it. Viewers suggest removing it, but ND tested that and says it is a detour, because it carries a lot of power.

posts.title_en: Suffering from power gaps? Know this
posts.summary_en: ND러너 explains the power correction (보정) system: it is not a nerf; team damage scales with the displayed power. That is why GingerBright on Coward backfires: a low-rarity cookie drags team power down, which acts like a whole-team ATK debuff. Arena applies only some growth sources, so power doesn't predict arena wins, but on stages power is honest and decides progress.

builds.gear: Always-good options on any server: Skill AMP, Skill Haste, DMG Reduction. Next: crit rate and crit damage. Server-dependent: focus and accuracy.
builds.why: Gear options change power a lot, so equal power doesn't mean equal strength.

mechanics: Correction (보정) system: not a nerf to cookies. 'The higher the power shown on screen, the higher the whole team's damage.'
GingerBright on Coward reduces enemy ATK but, being low-grade, lowers team power and so has the same effect as a whole-team ATK reduction. ND doesn't recommend it.
Ways to raise power: Stellar Link (biggest), breakthrough, Fame, gnome research, gear enhancement, sugar runes.

Arena applies only part of growth (level-up, promotion, holding effects, collection, gear, plate enhancement, sugar runes), so a lower-power opponent can win. On stages, 'power is the spec itself', and it is rare to have high power and still fail to push.
disagreements: GingerBright on Coward: ND against (power loss) versus guide makers for (ATK-down debuff).

quotes.kr: [00:32] 보정 시스템이란 너프되는게 아닙니다 ... 전투력이 높을수록 쿠키들의 딜이 비례에서 높아지는 현상이라고 보시면 됩니다
quotes.en: The correction system isn't a nerf; the higher your power, the more your cookies' damage rises in proportion.

quotes.en: The moment you add GingerBright, overall team power drops a lot, which works like an ATK reduction.

posts.title_en: Cool Mint? Coward? Every stage in one guide
posts.summary_en: 서신우's pre-relief all-stage guide (covering up to 168, before Princess Bari). Five decks (Witch, Devil, GingerBright, Biker, Licorice) and a per-map walkthrough of the eight repeating maps with difficulty ranks and boss tactics (Cool Mint, Coward, Bikers, Truck, Charles, spirits). Power advice: when stuck, check recommended power; once you're in the 35% bracket, spec up with gold and idle rewards. Kingdom Cool Mint, the hardest boss, is clearable exactly at 55% if everything goes right. Here 바궁 means Wind Archer.

clears.retries: retry on a bad first tornado
clears.note: 'If you succeed at all of it, it clears exactly at 55% of recommended power; each failure raises the requirement.'

cookies.note: '위치' in the caption.

teams.formation: Stay still after entry; moving loses damage. Retry only if the frontline dies.

builds.sugar_runes: Dealers: obvious damage lines. Healers: Skill Haste/AMP. Debuffers: about two lines of focus (집중). Low-grade cookies (e.g. GingerBright): HP/DMG Reduction survival lines.
builds.gear: Accuracy/focus: at Special grade and below take them if the stat rises. Consider options from Unique grade up. Some skip them and push with spec.

mechanics: [01:00] When stuck, look at the recommended power. Once you're in the 35% bracket, use gold and idle rewards to spec up.
Oven Wanderer: high grade, bad performance; tower/daily only. Never use it instead of Wind Archer.
Scorpion (정갈) is 'the best cookie in the game' and irreplaceable, as are Pomegranate and Milk. Wind Archer (바공) is good but replaceable by a same-synergy dealer or healer.
The maps cycle 들판 → 해변 → 도시 → 사막 → 숲 → 왕국 → 용암 → 설원 with rising difficulty. Difficulty order (hardest first): 왕국, 도시, 설원, 해변, 들판, 숲, 사막, 용암.
stage_types: 들판 x-30 Cool Mint: move to the lower-left diagonal and release when it jumps. Whether cookies stay or scatter is luck. Devil deck at low stages, GingerBright deck when survival fails. Choco-type bosses: Devil deck.
해변: the same as 들판, but the frontline Herb may die on mob maps; let it, or add a survival pet at the back.

도시 x-10 Bikers: all three must die. If they run in different directions you time out, so reroll until they move together downward. 도시 x-20 Truck: Devil deck; move opposite to dodge the first charge, then stand still and it comes to you. 도시 x-30 Coward: GingerBright deck; hit it on first contact to apply ATK-down, keep Scorpion on it as it moves, aim for about 50% HP at the fear phase, retry if cookies die at the first contact or fear return.
사막: a farming map. Eagle or 폭파광: Devil deck for single, Biker deck for groups.
숲 x-20/30 spirits: Licorice deck, stand still.

왕국 x-20 Charles: Devil deck. Hold in place, stick Scorpion to the boss at its 2nd/3rd auto for max early stacks. 왕국 x-30 Cool Mint: the hardest boss; stay in place (retry if the first tornado scatters you); refresh Scorpion poison before each tornado, keep Devil's shred up, and heal well or die at the third tornado; late adds must not steal the poison. Clears exactly at 55%.
용암: the easiest, auto. Devil deck only if x-20/x-30 time out.
설원: x-20 Devil deck. x-30 Coward: GingerBright deck.
disagreements: GingerBright deck for Coward and late Cool Mint (서신우) versus ND러너's no-GingerBright stance (yt:HyRdA_cEVcA, yt:tZJ5wzhcUA8). Note that this guide predates the 2026-09-23 relief.

posts.title_en: Idle deck for normal stages that works even past 300
posts.summary_en: 서신우 iterates an idle (auto) deck for normal multi-mob stages past 300. The base Bari deck fails on idle because Milk follows Bari forward and the backline loses Milk's buff. Bari goes out for Witchberry; Melon Soda goes out (it needs hugging); Dark Choco tested lower. Adding the Pierce (관통) synergy, Rockstar beat Strawberry Shortcake. For bosses swap Rockstar and Witchberry for Herb and Scorpion and hug; Cool Mint and Coward still use the old dedicated decks.

mechanics: On auto, Milk follows Bari forward, so the backline stops receiving Milk's buff. Manual play hides this.
Melon Soda, like Scorpion, needs to hug the target, so it is worthless on idle.

Bosses: swap to Herb + Scorpion and hug.
Cool Mint and Coward: the old dedicated decks.

posts.summary_en: A short update of the rapid-fire (연타) stage deck for Veteran-mercenary players, before Bari. Strawberry Crepe is the default since most stages need little shred. On single bosses switch to Dark Choco, and Milky Way to Scorpion. Brightseeker below 5★ → Scorpion or Wind Archer. Pets: Panda for airborne stages, a Choco pet or Icy Birdie for survival. posts.title_en: The final Coward guide, including how to read a clear
posts.summary_en: 꽝라멩's pre-relief Coward Cookie (비겁이) guide for players up to stage 190 and before mercenary Lv.4. The deck swaps Ion and Rye out for Scorpion and Skating Queen, because past 190 damage, not defence, was the bottleneck. The control technique is built around Scorpion's attack rhythm, and the video gives clear signals: debuff on first contact, all alive before fear, about 20 Scorpion stacks and boss at 50–55% HP at the fear phase.

teams.name: 꽝라멩 Coward deck
teams.for: 비겁한 쿠키 (Coward), up to about 190, mercenary below Lv.4

cookies.note: The deck funnels buffs to it.
'피결' in the caption.
The debuff must land at first contact.
Named with GingerBright as a debuff source.

teams.why: Past 190 defence can be solved by infinite retries, but damage can't, so Ion and Rye went out and the deck funnels into Scorpion.

mechanics: Scorpion attacks in threes: hit 1, a short pause, then hits 2 and 3 back to back. You can move right after hit 1, but not between hits 2 and 3.

Control: hit the boss immediately on contact so GingerBright's debuff lands before the heal (otherwise cookies die). Follow the moving boss and overlap Scorpion with it; re-stick after each 2–3 combo.
Clear signals: the debuff lands at the first contact; everyone is alive before the boss's fear; at fear time, about 20 Scorpion stacks and boss HP around 50–55%.
Overlapping the boss's floor attack while moving hurts a lot; in practice move on Scorpion's rhythm and hope.
'With time and more power it becomes easy anyway.'
stage_types: Coward: a mobile boss with fear and floor attacks; manual play.
disagreements: Uses GingerBright on Coward, which ND러너 advises against at higher stages.

quotes.kr: [00:00] 190스테이지 이후부터 방어가 부족한 부분은 무한 트라이로 해결할 수 있었는데 딜이 부족한 부분은 어찌할 방법이 없더라고요
quotes.en: After stage 190, missing defence can be solved with endless retries, but missing damage can't.

posts.title_en: No hands needed: idle stage deck recommendation
posts.summary_en: 꽝라멩's pre-relief idle stage setup: a general deck, an airborne-boss variant (Pinot in, Panda Dumpling pet instead of Icy Birdie) and a Coward deck. Milk is runed for ATK so it receives Passion Pay. Cake Hound keeps Strawberry Crepe and Cool Mint alive; scatter-shot cookies are excluded so idle play has no damage loss. Chargemellow is justified because Macaron, Rye, Strawberry Crepe and Herb all benefit from rapid-fire. A 2★ Brightseeker works, and the Milk/Cheesecake buff-overlap bug was fixed.

No captions exist (the video has no speech track captions), so the teams and positioning shown on screen are not extracted.
